director.chapterArc: A long, controlled passage from exclusion into conditional entry: Callie manages uncertainty by counting, endures the surrender of tools and mother, then defines herself truthfully on paper. Institutional coldness is repeatedly interrupted by small acts of care. The final blackout narrows the chapter into an intimate first contact with Toren, where news of Pitch’s careful burial quietly joins the two roads.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder grounded and observant. Let cold, wet clothing, bodily fatigue, and procedural detail carry the strain; do not sentimentalize the mother’s admission or inflate Meridian into spectacle. The late convergence should feel private and almost accidental, with grief held level enough that simple facts do the emotional work.

cues.delivery: Let the unexpected warmth soften the sterile procedure; receive the mother’s thanks and the guard’s changed voice without turning the moment sentimental.
cues.from: They did it where they stood, in the road, with a long canvas hose that came out through the gate. The water was warm. Nobody had told them it would be warm. They did all of them, one after another, and they did Callie's mother sitting on the tailboard. She lifted her face into it and shut her eyes, and when it was done she said, "Well, that was the first hot water I've had since the spring. Thank you." The grey coat holding the hose said, "You're welcome, ma'am," in a completely different voice from the one he had used about the ash.

cues.delivery: Keep the symptom list orderly and clinically exact, with decay contained inside practiced cataloguing; no vocal break or plea for pity.
cues.from: "My right hand," she said. "Since the end of the winter. It's got worse since the spring. It won't take instruction. Headaches, mornings, behind the left eye. Sick with them, sometimes. Fits. Three that I know of. The first one the morning of a causeway, a fortnight back. The last one five nights ago. A hundred and fifty-eight seconds. My daughter counted." She did not look at Callie. "My right leg, since the ninth day on the road, and worse since the last fit. I couldn't stand on it yesterday. And the words. I call things by the wrong names. I'm told. I don't always hear myself do it." She stopped. "I think that's all of it. It's all I've got written down."

cues.delivery: Give the forty paces grave, unhurried dignity. Hold Callie’s loss inside precise physical observation, allowing the shut gate and her raised arm to land without overt mourning.
cues.through: Callie stood in the road in her socks with her arm still up.
cues.reason: The mother’s solitary walk and disappearance form the chapter’s central separation.

cues.delivery: Pell speaks almost under the moment, offering certainty rather than consolation; keep the reassurance practical and quiet.
cues.from: "That's it," said Pell, beside her, very quietly. "That's the whole of it. She's in."
cues.through: "That's it," said Pell, beside her, very quietly. "That's the whole of it. She's in."
cues.reason: Pell steadies Callie immediately after the gate closes.

cues.delivery: Make the promised sequence sound usable, then place gentle weight on her mother walking in under her own power; avoid false optimism.
cues.from: "For about an hour," said Pell. "They'll have us in the next door along, and then they'll have us at a window, and then they'll give us a bed. You'll see her tomorrow." He paused. "She walked in, Callie. On her own feet, through that gate. That's in the book."
cues.through: "For about an hour," said Pell. "They'll have us in the next door along, and then they'll have us at a window, and then they'll give us a bed. You'll see her tomorrow." He paused. "She walked in, Callie. On her own feet, through that gate. That's in the book."
cues.reason: Pell turns helpless waiting into facts Callie can hold.

cues.delivery: Play the atlas reveal bone-dry: Callie’s literal objection meets Pell’s quiet, rule-lawyering competence. Do not brighten the voice broadly.
cues.from: "You haven't got the book. They took the book."
cues.through: "They took the ash," he said. "Nobody said anything about the book."
cues.reason: A restrained comic release follows the separation.

cues.delivery: Keep Hallet’s admission about his ‘bad face’ weary and deadpan, a tiny bureaucratic joke that does not soften the stakes.
cues.from: "Transient. Fourteen days, a grey band, no north yard. And a review, and I don't sit on the review." Hallet looked at her. "I've been told I say that part with a bad face. I've been trying not to."
cues.through: "Transient. Fourteen days, a grey band, no north yard. And a review, and I don't sit on the review." Hallet looked at her. "I've been told I say that part with a bad face. I've been trying not to."
cues.reason: Administrative self-awareness briefly punctures the tension.

cues.delivery: Let Ines state lifelong exclusion as an exhausted fact, without bitterness or invitation to comfort her.
cues.from: "I know," said Ines. "I've been in it all my life." She stepped back from the window and went and sat on the bench against the hot pipes, and put her quiver across her knees, and did not look at the cards again.
cues.through: "I know," said Ines. "I've been in it all my life." She stepped back from the window and went and sat on the bench against the hot pipes, and put her quiver across her knees, and did not look at the cards again.
cues.reason: Her dry reply exposes the human cost of the register’s largest category.

cues.delivery: Read the limits like survival specifications. Tighten slightly toward ‘I’m dry,’ but keep Callie’s fear converted into exact, honest data.
cues.from: Ninety-one seconds was everything I had.
cues.through: I can't do any of it at present. I'm dry.
cues.reason: The card reaches the decisive admission that her power is unavailable.

cues.delivery: Treat the added line with protective respect for Callie’s self-knowledge. Keep it plain; its truth matters more than its pathos.
cues.from: She looked at the last line for a long time. Then, at the very bottom, in smaller letters, she added one more.
cues.through: She did not know why she added it. It was not a capability. But it was the truest thing on the card, and she was not going to cross it out.
cues.reason: Callie names counting as the capability beneath all her others.

cues.delivery: Allow a small break in Hallet’s routine: professional respect, not paternal reassurance. Keep his warning about how cards are read candid and unsweetened.
cues.from: "I'll tell them you asked," he said. He laid the card down on the desk in front of him, face up, square to the edge. "It's a true card. That's the second one I've had this month that says at present. I'd rather have one card like that than ten good ones." He wrote something in the book. "And I'll tell you something for nothing, which I'm not supposed to. Nobody reads the first line first. They read the one they're looking for. But I'll tell them you asked."

cues.delivery: Give the red thread and its invisible weight quiet significance; this is entry made tangible, not triumph.
cues.from: Then there were bands. They were paper, and they went round the wrist and fastened, and two of them had a red thread run through the paper. Hallet pushed them through the hatch one at a time and said each name as he did. Callie's had a red thread in it. She put it on her right wrist. It was the lightest thing she had ever been given that she knew was heavy.

cues.delivery: Carry Toren’s line softly across the blackout, level with exhaustion and offered only because darkness has removed the need to look at each other.
cues.from: "It does that every night," said the boy, across the dark. His voice was quiet and very tired. "At the first hour. They've got a written reason."
cues.through: "It does that every night," said the boy, across the dark. His voice was quiet and very tired. "At the first hour. They've got a written reason."
cues.reason: The first contact between the two roads begins in shared darkness.

cues.delivery: Callie offers the roadside fact tentatively, without yet knowing its value; prepare the name as the reason the silence suddenly matters.
cues.from: "There's a mule," said Callie. "Out on the big road. By the rail. Somebody buried it. There's a board on a stake." She did not know why she was telling him. It came out, the way things came out of her in silences, the way her mother had always said they did. "It says Pitch."
cues.through: "There's a mule," said Callie. "Out on the big road. By the rail. Somebody buried it. There's a board on a stake." She did not know why she was telling him. It came out, the way things came out of her in silences, the way her mother had always said they did. "It says Pitch."
cues.reason: Pitch’s name reveals the hidden connection between Callie and Toren.

cues.delivery: Hold Toren’s voice unnaturally level. Let the dry description of Pitch protect him from saying what the mule meant; do not let grief break through theatrically.
cues.from: "He pulled a cart three hundred miles," said the boy at last. His voice was very level, in the way a voice is when somebody is holding it there. "He was nine hundred pounds of extremely disagreeable animal. I asked somebody to get him off the road."
cues.through: "He pulled a cart three hundred miles," said the boy at last. His voice was very level, in the way a voice is when somebody is holding it there. "He was nine hundred pounds of extremely disagreeable animal. I asked somebody to get him off the road."
cues.reason: Toren receives confirmation of Pitch’s death and burial.

cues.delivery: Callie answers with the concrete workmanship of the grave, intuitively giving him proof that Pitch was treated as someone’s responsibility.
cues.from: "Somebody did," said Callie. "Somebody dug it square. And they painted the board."
cues.through: "Somebody did," said Callie. "Somebody dug it square. And they painted the board."
cues.reason: The square grave and painted board become an act of carried kindness.

cues.delivery: Make the thanks quiet, deliberate, and costly; Toren can acknowledge the kindness but cannot remain for more.
cues.from: "Thank you," he said, from the doorway. "For telling me."
cues.through: "Thank you," he said, from the doorway. "For telling me."
cues.reason: Toren’s restrained gratitude closes their first exchange.

cues.delivery: Return to Callie’s measured inventory of unresolved things. Let each institutional location widen her solitude, ending on suspended review rather than despair.
cues.from: Then the door closed, and Callie sat alone on her step in the dark, in a place that had written everything down, with her mother in a long building somewhere at the north end of it and her hook in a bin with a paper tag on the handle, and her card on a desk somewhere, face up, square to the edge, waiting for somebody else to look at it.
